## Natural history notes

A large leaf-footed bug characterized by its elongated brown body, long antennae, and flattened expansions on the hind legs, with darker markings near the rear of the abdomen. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, hammocks, parks, and other areas with shrubs, trees, vines, or herbaceous plants. It feeds by piercing plant tissue and sucking sap from stems, fruits, seeds, and new growth, while also serving as prey for birds, spiders, assassin bugs, and other insect-eating animals.
